result:
I've written the round-303 task: **NAME-AND-HINT-b** (Saba's Q5, the one-time "Drag a clip by its name bar to move it." hint). Decision is **CONTINUE**. Round 302 passed and was published, and nothing external is blocking.

**Round 302 result**
- C passed all 21 rows with 0 bugs, checked in a real browser at both viewports.
- One row, the purchased-workspace heading, is BLOCKED because the backend isn't available in the cloud. Unit tests cover it.
- Gate 302 published `1fd0129` to both remotes, and that is the baseline for round 303. NAME-AND-HINT-a is done.
- A's code-reviewer Low and gate finding 2 have the same root cause: the new repo-wide name-check test is both too narrow and would fail on a TODO comment. I merged them into one deferred Low. Gate finding 3, the stale "Personal Studio" e2e expectation, is attached to the existing record. The rest is logged as info.
- The backlog is now version 262, with decisions D-29z788 to D-29z792, and `feature-status.md` is updated.

**Round 303 task**
- **What changes:** the first successful library add appends Saba's sentence to the "added" status, in the same status write. That covers Enter, the library add actions, the preview's Add button and drag-drop.
  - Refused adds and video imports neither show the hint nor use it up.
  - Undo doesn't bring it back.
  - It shows once each time the Studio page is opened in a tab: a reload, or leaving and re-entering the Studio, shows it again.
  - On a source with a BPM, the hint sits between the "added" sentence and the existing tempo text.
- **Reference:** the Live 12 manual confirms the behaviour we already have. Only the clip bar moves a clip (§6.7), and dragging in the clip body selects time (§6.9). Live has no such hint; this one exists because Saba asked for it in Q5.
- **Advice used:** product-designer chose the same-write delivery, the triggers and the per-load lifetime. I adjusted it for the tempo text, which it didn't know about. The advisor was available and consulted twice, and I applied all its points.
- **My dry run on a scratch copy:**
  - The change makes 12 existing exact-text assertions fail, in 5 test files. All 12 are granted to A, with the rule that no assertion is lost; the other 172 files pass.
  - In a HEAD browser probe, the longest status with the hint is 1162 px of the 1256 px available at 1280×720, so it stays on one line and the footer height doesn't change.
- **Changes A must make:** 9 paths. The two source files must match my sketch byte for byte. A adds a new test file (NB1–NB9), runs mutants m1–m5 and a code review, and sets implementation doc 221 to `Completed (C round 303 PASS)`.
- **C checks:** each hint path; the seed text (waiting for it to appear); body drag vs name-bar drag; status-line height; screen-reader output; screen budget; the full journey; auth. All at 1440×900 and 1280×720.
- **New Saba question:** `SABA-Q-NAME-HINT-LIFETIME`, asking whether the hint should stop after the first visit in this browser. The default is no, and it doesn't block anything.

**Next:** round 304 is PERF-3c, round 305 is RETRO, and the next regression round is due on 2026-11-05. The frontend-architect checkpoint request is still unanswered and doesn't block; I added one new input to it.

I wrote only to the loop folder and a `/tmp` scratch copy, and the store tree is still clean at `1fd0129`.
